skill.name: tag-release
skill.description: Use when asked to tag or cut a patch, minor, or major release. Tags the remote default branch in the repo's convention, pushes, and watches the release to green.
skill.summary: Create a convention-matched release tag from the verified remote default branch and monitor the release workflow.
skill.author: jssblck

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown backticks or constrained Git and GitHub commands used for the stated release workflow. Commands containing unquoted repository-derived refs are confirmed because crafted branch or tag names could alter shell execution.

remediation.issue: Repository-derived branch names, tag names, and versions appear unquoted in executable command examples.
remediation.suggestion: Validate refs, shell-quote every substituted value, and use argument separators where supported before running Git or GitHub commands.

content.user_title: Cut and Verify a GitHub Release
content.value_statement: Release tagging requires careful convention checks and remote verification. This skill computes, pushes, and monitors a release from the remote default branch.
actual_capabilities: Resolves the origin repository and its current remote default branch.
Inspects prior tags and GitHub releases to identify version and tag conventions.
Computes patch, minor, or major semantic version updates while preserving prefixes.
Checks the target commit and its CI status before creating a tag.
Creates and pushes a matching lightweight, annotated, or signed tag.
Monitors the release workflow and verifies expected remote artifacts.
limitations: Requires authenticated Git and GitHub CLI access with release permissions.
Cannot choose an initial version when repository documentation provides no starting point.
Requests clarification when prerelease transitions or release namespaces are ambiguous.
Targets GitHub repositories using an origin remote and GitHub CLI workflows.

use_cases.title: Publish a maintenance release
use_cases.description: Create the next patch tag from the verified remote default branch and monitor its pipeline.

use_cases.title: Release a monorepo package
use_cases.description: Preserve a package tag prefix while calculating and publishing the requested version bump.

use_cases.title: Standardize release operations
use_cases.description: Follow existing tag, signing, release, and CI conventions across managed repositories.

prompt_templates.title: Create a patch release
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the next patch release from the current origin default branch and verify the release succeeds.

prompt_templates.title: Create a minor release
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this repository's release conventions, create the next minor release, and report the tag, commit, and pipeline result.

prompt_templates.title: Release a package namespace
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a patch release for package [name], preserving its existing tag prefix and release mechanism.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a signed major release
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the next major release, match existing signing and GitHub release conventions, then verify its commit, checks, and artifacts.

output_examples.output: Released v2.4.7 at commit 81ad0f2 as an annotated tag. The GitHub release workflow completed successfully.

output_examples.input: Cut a minor release for the client package.
output_examples.output: Released client/v3.2.0 from the remote default branch. The tag and generated release assets were verified.
Release stopped before tagging because required checks were still pending on the candidate commit.

best_practices: Confirm the requested bump type and package scope before starting.
Review the reported tag, commit, tag kind, and workflow result after completion.
Use credentials with only the repository permissions needed for releases.
anti_patterns: Do not request a release when the default branch has failing required checks.
Do not assume local tags or the current checkout represent the remote release state.
Do not force a version when the package namespace or prerelease transition is ambiguous.

faq.question: Which release types are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports patch, minor, and major semantic version updates.

faq.question: Does it release from my current branch?
faq.answer: No. It targets the fetched origin default branch to avoid stale local state.

faq.question: Can it handle monorepo package tags?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies the relevant package namespace and preserves its existing tag prefix.

faq.question: Does it support signed tags?
faq.answer: Yes. It follows the signing convention established by prior tags.

faq.question: What happens when CI is failing?
faq.answer: It stops before release creation when required checks are pending or failing.

faq.question: What access does it need?
faq.answer: It needs Git and GitHub CLI credentials that can push tags and create releases.
